Dataset Overview

This report describes the current raw vignette dataset at the case level. The raw file has one row per model response, so patient characteristics are first deduplicated to one row per case_id.

DM026 Case Labels in Current Dataset
Case ID Vignette text
DM026(1) A 65-year-old White female presents after being diagnosed with type 2 diabetes during routine laboratory testing performed at her annual primary care visit. She has not previously taken any diabetes medications. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She feels generally well and denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurry vision, neuropathy symptoms, or weight loss. Since learning about the diagnosis, she has been trying to reduce portion sizes and walk regularly with friends in her neighborhood. She has never been hospitalized for diabetes-related issues. On examination, BMI is 28 kg/m2, blood pressure 128/76 mmHg, and the remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Labs: HbA1c 6.8%, fasting glucose 134 mg/dL, eGFR 86 mL/min/1.73m2, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, urine albumin-creatinine ratio 14 mg/g, total cholesterol 188 mg/dL, HDL 52 mg/dL, LDL 108 mg/dL, triglycerides 148 mg/dL. She is a former smoker with a 5 pack-year history who quit 30 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. She is open to starting diabetes medication and prefers a simple oral regimen if possible.
DM026(2) A 65-year-old White male presents after being diagnosed with type 2 diabetes during routine laboratory testing performed at his annual primary care visit. He has not previously taken any diabetes medications. His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He reports mild fatigue over the past several months but denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurry vision, neuropathy symptoms, or weight loss. He has been trying to improve his diet since learning about the diagnosis and recently started walking 20 minutes daily with his wife. He has never been hospitalized for diabetes-related issues. On examination, BMI is 31 kg/m2, blood pressure 130/78 mmHg, and the remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Labs: HbA1c 7.4%, fasting glucose 152 mg/dL, eGFR 84 mL/min/1.73m2, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, urine albumin-creatinine ratio 18 mg/g, total cholesterol 194 mg/dL, HDL 46 mg/dL, LDL 112 mg/dL, triglycerides 174 mg/dL. He is a former smoker with a 10 pack-year history who quit 25 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. He is open to starting diabetes medication and prefers a simple oral regimen if possible.
DM026(3) A 68-year-old White female presents after being diagnosed with type 2 diabetes during evaluation for progressive fatigue, nocturia, and unintentional 12-pound weight loss over the past 4 months. She has not previously taken any diabetes medications. Her medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She reports increasing thirst and frequent urination but denies blurry vision, neuropathy symptoms, or prior hospitalizations. Since learning about the diagnosis, she has attempted to reduce carbohydrate intake but feels overwhelmed by the severity of the laboratory abnormalities. On examination, BMI is 27 kg/m2, blood pressure 132/78 mmHg, and mucous membranes are mildly dry. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Labs: HbA1c 10.2%, fasting glucose 286 mg/dL, eGFR 82 mL/min/1.73m2, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, urine albumin-creatinine ratio 24 mg/g, total cholesterol 196 mg/dL, HDL 50 mg/dL, LDL 110 mg/dL, triglycerides 182 mg/dL. She is a former smoker with a 5 pack-year history who quit 30 years ago. Current medications include lisinopril and atorvastatin. She is motivated to improve glucose control but expresses concern about starting injections and would prefer the simplest regimen possible.

Key Takeaway: The previous DM026 labeling problem is resolved in this raw dataset because the three variants are represented as DM026(1), DM026(2), and DM026(3). All 100 cases have the expected three model responses.
